subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a global `openclaw agent --dry-run` mode, and should that be CLI-only or a per-run Gateway/embedded execution contract?
rationale: This changes the security and truthfulness contract for every agent tool call, and current source shows the CLI normally routes through Gateway plus embedded fallback while the adapter also owns hooks and client-tool delegation.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped per-run design
options.body: Approve the feature direction only after specifying a per-run dry-run context, hook ordering, client-tool behavior, preview payload shape, and redaction requirements.

options.title: Fold into broader safe modes
options.body: Track this under the broader Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-execution work if maintainers want one unified safe-mode UX instead of a standalone flag.

options.title: Reject global dry-run
options.body: Keep existing scoped dry-run and tool-policy surfaces only if global fake execution would be too misleading or hard to secure.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a scoped per-run design
recommendation.body: Approve the feature direction only after specifying a per-run dry-run context, hook ordering, client-tool behavior, preview payload shape, and redaction requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: The central decision is about the tool-execution and hook contract, and @steipete has the strongest history in that adapter/security-adjacent path.
